title: NUMA-aware KV micro-sharding and hot-key replication for continuous batching
creator: Anika Patel
description: Goal: Reduce tail latency and GPU memory overhead for long-context continuous-batching workloads by splitting KV cache into fine-grained NUMA-aware micro-shards, with lightweight hot-key replication across adjacent GPU memory slabs. This ticket implements a coordinated placement and replication strategy so that frequently accessed KV slices (hot keys) are available locally on the serving GPU while cold slices remain partitioned to save memory and avoid unnecessary duplication. The design targets mixed tensor/pipeline parallel topologies and low-latency single-request streaming workloads.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integration test demonstrating <5% median latency increase and 25-35% reduction in cross-GPU KV fetches on representative continuous-batching trace compared to baseline
Memory accounting shows at most 10% extra GPU memory overhead for replication under realistic hot-key distributions
Eviction and consisency tests validate no correctness regressions for KV state across pipeline stages
Automated canary rollout config + console metric dashboards for per-slab local-hit-rate published
technical_notes: Micro-shard granularity: 64KB logical slices mapped to GPU slab IDs; mapping table maintained in host pinned memory and replicated to all participating GPUs for fast lookup
NUMA-aware placement: prefer mapping hot micro-shards to GPU whose PCIe/NVLink topology has lowest hop-count to originating host thread; fallback to nearest peer using topology matrix
Hot-key replication: opportunistic shallow replication (single-copy extra) using async RDMA/NVLink memcpy; replication decays via LFU heuristic with time-decay tau tuned per workload
Consistency model: eventual with bounded staleness for reads during continuous batching; write-through on model-generated KV updates to primary shard and background async replication to replicas
Eviction policy: two-tier LRU where local slab evicts cold micro-shards first and signals home-owner shard for potential re-fetch from primary
Integration with pipeline parallelism: shard ownership assigned at tensor-slice level aligned with pipeline stage boundaries to avoid cross-stage KV fetches during autoregressive generation

decisions: Adopt 64KB micro-shard size as trade-off between lookup overhead and replication granularity
Use LFU with exponential time decay rather than pure LRU to identify hot keys in continuous-batching traces
Bounded-staleness reads accepted for performance; writes are serialized to primary shard and propagated asynchronously
